issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires a modifiable List<Meal> attribute named 'orders' (and even shows this in the UML), but the provided solution implements 'orders' as a Meal[] array. The template and helper classes also use arrays (ArrayHelpers), which conflicts with the textual requirement of a List and the UML. This mismatch can confuse students about whether to use a List or an array and whether they should rely on ArrayHelpers utilities or Java Collections.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and starter code consistent: either change the problem statement and UML to require an array-based 'orders' (Meal[]) and mention ArrayHelpers, or update the template and solution to use a modifiable List<Meal> (e.g., ArrayList) throughout. Ensure example code and UML match the chosen representation.

issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting guidance about the 'stock' attribute: it first describes a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (implying an instance-final field), but later states that the 'stock' attribute must be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is a conceptual mismatch and will confuse students whether to implement an instance final field or a static shared field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: explicitly state that 'stock' is a static (and optionally final) field shared by all SealSaloon instances, or remove the static requirement and require an instance final field initialized in the constructor. Update the UML and text to consistently reflect the chosen design (static shared stock vs instance stock).
